# computesphere_web_service (Resource)

Manages a web service in an environment: a service with a public address, deployed from a container image or built from a git repository.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    computesphere = {
      source  = "computesphere/computesphere"
      version = "~> 1.1"
    }
  }
}

variable "api_token" {
  description = "API token for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "account_id" {
  description = "Account ID for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
}

variable "api_url" {
  description = "API URL for ComputeSphere"
  type        = string
  default     = "api.computesphere.com"
}

provider "computesphere" {
  api_token  = var.api_token  # or set COMPUTESPHERE_API_TOKEN env variable
  account_id = var.account_id # or set COMPUTESPHERE_ACCOUNT_ID env variable
  api_url    = var.api_url    # or set COMPUTESPHERE_API_URL env variable
}

resource "computesphere_web_service" "app" {
  service_id     = var.service_id
  environment_id = var.environment_id
  project_id     = var.project_id

  image        = "nginx:1.27"
  port         = 8080
  sphere_count = 2

  env_vars = {
    LOG_LEVEL = "info"
  }
  secret_vars = {
    API_KEY = var.api_key
  }

  health_check = {
    enabled = true
    path    = "/healthz"
  }

  autoscaling = {
    enabled         = true
    min_replicas    = 2
    max_replicas    = 6
    cpu_utilization = 70
  }
}

# Built from a git repository.
resource "computesphere_web_service" "web" {
  service_id     = var.web_service_id
  environment_id = var.environment_id
  project_id     = var.project_id

  git_url           = "acme/web"
  branch            = "main"
  git_connection_id = var.git_connection_id
  runtime_type      = "native"
  language          = "nodejs"
  version           = "20"
  build_command     = "npm ci && npm run build"
  start_command     = "npm start"
  port              = 3000
  predeploy_command = "npm run migrate"

  # Public values only: build args are baked into the image.
  build_args = {
    NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL = "https://api.example.com"
  }
}

variable "api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "git_connection_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "service_id" {
  description = "Service this resource runs"
  type        = string
}

variable "environment_id" {
  description = "Environment to run it in"
  type        = string
}

variable "project_id" {
  description = "Project the service belongs to"
  type        = string
}

variable "web_service_id" {
  description = "Service the git-built web service runs"
  type        = string
}

output "url" {
  value = computesphere_web_service.app.url
}

# Moving from computesphere_deployment: replace the old resource block with
# this one and keep a moved block. Terraform carries the deployment over
# without redeploying it.
moved {
  from = computesphere_deployment.app
  to   = computesphere_web_service.app
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment the web service runs in. Changing it creates a new web service.
- `project_id` (String) Project the service belongs to. Changing it creates a new web service.
- `service_id` (String) Service this web service runs; its name and plan are taken from the service. Changing it creates a new web service.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `autoscaling` (Attributes) CPU autoscaling between a fewest and a most spherelets. Team plan and above. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling))
- `branch` (String) Branch to build and to deploy on push.
- `build_args` (Map of String) Docker build args. Public values only: they are baked into the image, so secrets belong in `secret_vars`.
- `build_command` (String) Build command.
- `context` (String) Docker build context directory.
- `deploy_policy` (String) Deploy policy: `auto` or `approval`. Leave it out to use the environment's policy. Setting it needs the project admin role.
- `dockerfile` (String) Dockerfile path of a Docker build.
- `env_vars` (Map of String) Plain environment variables, name to value. Changing them redeploys.
- `git_connection_id` (String) Git connection that clones the repository and delivers pushes.
- `git_repo_id` (String) The repository's id at its git provider, e.g. a GitLab project id. Needed for GitLab sources. Sent at create, and read back. If the web service has none at ComputeSphere (e.g. one created without it), setting it only records it here. Removing it from the configuration keeps the recorded value, and a value that differs from the web service's is refused at plan time, because the API can't change it.
- `git_url` (String) Repository to build from. Set this or `image`.
- `health_check` (Attributes) HTTP health check. A spherelet that fails it is taken out of traffic. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--health_check))
- `image` (String) Container image to deploy, e.g. `nginx:1.27`. Set this or `git_url`.
- `image_password` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Registry password or token of a private image. Write-only: it is sent to the API and never stored in state or plan (Terraform 1.11 or later). To rotate it, set the new value and increase `image_password_wo_version`.
- `image_password_wo_version` (Number) Version of `image_password`. Increase it to send a new password; the change applies in place. Setting it for the first time on an imported or moved resource only records it.
- `image_provider` (String) Registry provider of a private image, e.g. `docker`, `azure`, `other` or `custom`.
- `image_type` (String) `public` (the default) or `private`. A private image is pulled with `image_provider`, `image_username`, `image_password` and `image_url`.
- `image_url` (String) Registry endpoint of a private image. Needed for providers that sign in with a username and password.
- `image_username` (String) Registry username of a private image.
- `language` (String) Managed toolchain of a native build, e.g. `nodejs`, `python` or `go`.
- `network_access` (Attributes) Who can reach the web service. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_access))
- `port` (Number) Port the service listens on. Defaults to 8080.
- `predeploy_command` (String) Command run before each new version starts serving, e.g. database migrations. Changing it creates a new web service.
- `root_dir` (String) The service's directory in a monorepo.
- `runtime_type` (String) Build mode of a git source: `native` (a managed toolchain set by `language`) or `docker` (a Dockerfile). Derived from the source when left out.
- `secret_vars` (Map of String, Sensitive) Secret environment variables, name to value. Changing them redeploys.
- `sphere_count` (Number) Spherelets to run. Defaults to 1. Changing it scales in place.
- `start_command` (String) Start command of a git build.
- `tag_pattern` (String) Glob a tag must match to build when `trigger_on` is `tag`, e.g. `v*`.
- `trigger_on` (String) What a git push must be to build: `branch` (pushes to `branch`, the default) or `tag` (tags matching `tag_pattern`).
- `version` (String) Language version of a native build, e.g. `20` for Node.js.
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Wait for the web service to finish deploying after create and change.
- `watch_paths` (List of String) gitignore-style globs; a push builds only when a changed file matches one. Defaults to `root_dir`, else every push.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Deployment id of the web service.
- `internal_url` (String) Address other services in the same environment use.
- `name` (String) Name, taken from the service.
- `status` (String) Current status.
- `url` (String) Public address.

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Turn autoscaling on or off.

Optional:

- `cpu_utilization` (Number) CPU percentage to scale at.
- `max_replicas` (Number) Most spherelets.
- `min_replicas` (Number) Fewest spherelets.


<a id="nestedatt--health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `health_check`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Turn the check on or off.

Optional:

- `initial_delay_seconds` (Number) Seconds before the first probe (0-300). Defaults to 10.
- `path` (String) HTTP path probed. Required while `enabled` is true.
- `period_seconds` (Number) Seconds between probes (0-300). Defaults to 30.
- `port` (Number) Port probed; leave it out to probe the service port.
- `readiness_failure_threshold` (Number) Failures in a row before a spherelet is taken out of traffic (0-20); 0 uses the platform default of 3.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Probe timeout in seconds (0-60); 0 uses the platform default of 3.


<a id="nestedatt--network_access"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_access`

Required:

- `type` (String) `public_access`, or `restricted_access` to allow only `whitelisted_ips`.

Optional:

- `default_url_disabled` (Boolean) Turn off the default ComputeSphere address. Needs a verified custom domain that is serving.
- `whitelisted_ips` (List of String) Addresses or CIDR ranges allowed in when `type` is `restricted_access`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = computesphere_web_service.app
  id = "d1a2b3c4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by deployment ID
terraform import computesphere_web_service.app d1a2b3c4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab
```
